occupations.cat: Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians

n.story:
Your role is shifting from a manual laborer to a high-tech site orchestrator. While the physical act of laying bricks or installing wood elements remains a human craft due to the unpredictable nature of construction sites, the 'mental' load of the job is being revolutionized. You no longer spend hours squinting at paper blueprints or cross-referencing thick binders of building codes; instead, AI-powered tablets and AR glasses overlay digital twins onto the physical site, instantly flagging compliance issues or material mismatches before a single nail is driven.

As AI takes over the tedious tasks of structural inspection and material compatibility simulations, you are freed to focus on complex problem-solving and high-level project coordination. You will spend more time using generative design tools to optimize floor plans for energy efficiency and less time on repetitive administrative checks. Your value lies in your ability to manage the 'physical-digital' interface—ensuring that the precision of AI-driven planning is successfully executed by the human team in the messy, real-world environment of a building site.

Routine concrete and structural crack detection
amp: Real-time supply chain and alternative material sourcing
Generative design for optimized house layouts
Precision site layout using AI-driven CAD tools
Enhanced hazard detection via wearable safety sensors
Predictive maintenance scheduling for construction structures
tools: Computer vision drones for site inspection
n.adv: Master AI-integrated BIM software and practice using AR tools for site visualization; your future value depends on being the bridge between digital precision and physical craftsmanship.

n.story:
Your presence on the job site remains indispensable, but your 'eyes' have become digital. Instead of manually tracking progress with a clipboard and planning shifts on a spreadsheet, you now oversee a fleet of drones and IoT sensors that feed real-time data into your dashboard. AI handles the logistical headaches of employee scheduling and inventory processing, freeing you to focus on high-level problem solving and site safety. 

You have evolved into a 'predictive manager.' By using AI to simulate material compatibility and feasibility, you can spot structural or supply chain issues months before they manifest. Your role shifts from reactive firefighting to proactive optimization, particularly in green building practices where AI helps you calculate the most sustainable and cost-effective paths forward. You lead your crew with better data, ensuring deadlines are met through algorithmic precision rather than just sheer willpower.
